1235.title: JavaScript: expose provenance-preserving categorical evidence assessment for legal reasoning
1235.body:
The JavaScript relative meta-logic component at fd5bfaced85262a51b341fb2b25c79e507423ca3 aggregates probabilistic evidence, but legal source absence, contradictions and contextual applicability need an explicit categorical interface.

Downstream work: https://github.com/link-assistant/legal/pull/2 (issue https://github.com/link-assistant/legal/issues/1).

Proposed addition: assessLegalContext(evidence) returning supported / contradicted / conflict / unknown, with provenance labels. Empty input must remain unknown; opposing source stances must remain a conflict. A probability must not be presented as proof of legal validity.

We are developing a patch against js/agentic/crate/relative_meta_logic.mjs in the downstream PR, kept as a patch with the pinned source checksum, and deterministic tests for exceptions, missing facts, dates, jurisdiction, conflicting rules and source drift. Executable rules require reviewed semantics and exact source spans. Surface modal extraction is explicitly unverified. This does not claim to solve arbitrary legal reasoning.

Upstream incorporation would remove the temporary patch and support other deterministic applications. Broader automatic semantic formalization of legislation remains an unresolved capability requirement.

1330.title: Detect that two questions have the same meaning with different wording (sameMeaning(a, b))
1330.body:
# Feature request: `sameMeaning(a, b)` — detect that two questions have the same meaning with different wording

## Context

[meta-sovereign](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign) (a local, open-source messenger client) learns which questions were asked in a conversation and wants to treat questions with the same meaning but different wording as one (its requirement R-Y54). We tried the latest formal-ai locally for this; the examples below are synthetic.

## Summary

formal-ai has no API for comparing two arbitrary natural-language questions and deciding whether they convey the same intent. A `sameMeaning(a, b) -> { same: boolean, confidence: number }` function is needed, working for both Russian and English.

## Commit

`98f7808d49583e1e7932d133355445d8fdfb91f9` (default branch at time of evaluation)

## Environment

- OS: macOS Darwin 24.6.0 (arm64)
- Rust: 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13), installed via `rustup toolchain install 1.99`
- Node: v24.18.0
- formal-ai version: 0.355.0

## Exact commands

```bash
# build (one-time):
rustup toolchain install 1.99
rustup override set 1.99   # inside formal-ai repo
cargo +1.99 run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai -- --help

# per-prompt test used:
cargo +1.99 run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai -- \
  chat --prompt "На вы?" --format text --silent
```

No dedicated same-meaning endpoint exists. The evaluation ran each prompt individually via `chat` and compared the raw text outputs.

## Expected vs actual for each pair

| # | Prompt A | Prompt B | Expected | A response (summary) | B response (summary) | Result |
|---|----------|----------|----------|----------------------|----------------------|--------|
| 1 | "На вы?" | "Можно к вам на вы обращаться?" | same | lookup failure (no cached data for "На вы") | unknown rule | FAIL — routes to different handlers |
| 2 | "Можно на ты?" | "Давай на ты?" | same | lookup failure (topic "Можно") | lookup failure (topic "Давай") | FAIL — different lookup keys, same underlying intent ignored |
| 3 | "Where do you work?" | "What company are you at?" | same | lookup failure (no cached data) | self-identity response: "I am formal-ai…" | FAIL — completely different routes |
| 4 | "Кем ты работаешь?" | "Чем занимаешься по работе?" | same | unknown | unknown | FAIL — both unknown, equivalence not detected |
| 5 | "Do you have a LinkedIn?" | "Can you send me your LinkedIn profile?" | same | unknown | **misroutes to `list_dir`** capability | FAIL — wrong route on B; intent not recognised |
| 6 | "Когда созвонимся?" | "В какое время удобно поговорить?" | same | unknown | unknown | FAIL — both unknown, equivalence not detected |
| 7 | "На вы?" | "На ты?" | different | lookup failure "На вы" | lookup failure "На ты" | ACCIDENTAL PASS — different only because lookup keys differ, not due to semantic comparison |
| 8 | "Where do you work?" | "Where do you live?" | different | lookup failure "Where do you work" | lookup failure "Where do you live" | ACCIDENTAL PASS — same reason |
| 9 | "Когда созвонимся?" | "Зачем созваниваться?" | different | unknown | unknown | ACCIDENTAL PASS — both unknown; no semantic differentiation |

Summary: 0 of 9 pairs correctly handled by semantic reasoning. The 3 "different" pairs appear correct only by coincidence (the lookup key or the boilerplate intro differs); the system performs no actual equivalence comparison.

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai repo
cd repo
rustup toolchain install 1.99 && rustup override set 1.99
cargo +1.99 run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai -- \
  chat --prompt "Where do you work?" --format text --silent
# → "No captured provider response is available for `Where do you work`."

cargo +1.99 run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai -- \
  chat --prompt "What company are you at?" --format text --silent
# → "I am formal-ai, a deterministic symbolic AI implementation…"
```

These two questions mean the same thing but produce entirely different responses from different handlers.

A second sharp failure:

```bash
cargo +1.99 run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai -- \
  chat --prompt "Can you send me your LinkedIn profile?" --format text --silent
# → "This request routes to the `list_dir` capability, but this chat surface does not expose the required `shell` tool."
```

"Can you send me your LinkedIn profile?" is wrongly routed to `list_dir`.

## What API would help

A deterministic, symbolic `sameMeaning(a, b)` function that:

1. Formalises both inputs into intent frames using the existing meanings lexicon
   (`rust/src/seed/meanings.rs`) and the multilingual cue lexicon
   (`rust/src/cue_lexicon.rs`).
2. Compares the resulting frames structurally — same intent type, same
   subject slot, compatible argument types.
3. Returns `{ same: bool, confidence: f64, intent_a: String, intent_b: String }`
   so the caller can inspect the reasoning.
4. Works for at least Russian and English (the two main languages in the
   existing test matrix).

Suggested Rust signature:

```rust
pub fn same_meaning(a: &str, b: &str) -> SameMeaningResult;

pub struct SameMeaningResult {
    pub same: bool,
    pub confidence: f64,   // 0.0–1.0
    pub intent_a: String,  // canonical intent label for `a`
    pub intent_b: String,  // canonical intent label for `b`
}
```

Suggested CLI surface:

```bash
formal-ai same-meaning --a "Where do you work?" --b "What company are you at?"
# → { "same": true, "confidence": 0.92, "intent_a": "ask_employer", "intent_b": "ask_employer" }
```

And a corresponding HTTP endpoint:

```
POST /api/openai/v1/same-meaning
{ "a": "...", "b": "..." }
→ { "same": true, "confidence": 0.92, "intent_a": "...", "intent_b": "..." }
```

The existing `StatementSignature::with_semantic_terms` in
`rust/src/summarization/dedup.rs` and the `RouteIntent` logic in
`rust/src/capability_routing/` are good starting points: they already group
semantically equivalent phrasings for tool routing and statement deduplication.
Extending that logic to the general two-prompt case would close this gap without
neural inference.

1364.title: Hive Mind 2026-10-20 (0.354.1): Hello World via /claude, /codex and /agent all failed (branch 'so', web_run {} ×210, build outputs left, invalid gh flags, scalac missing, exit code misread, workflow never planned): everything the next release must fix
1364.body:
## Summary

On 2026-10-20 Hive Mind 2.39.2 ran the three Hello World issues with Formal AI **0.354.1** as the model, one per client. **None succeeded:**

| Client | Issue / PR | Execution | Result | What Formal AI produced in this run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code (`--tool claude`) | [Kotlin #1](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-fa49-7c9d-a664-b7ea33bb698a/issues/1) / [PR #2](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-fa49-7c9d-a664-b7ea33bb698a/pull/2) | `2719fb28` | **failed, exit 1** after 7 min 28 s | Session 1: correct `Main.kt`, verify script, compiled, ran, committed and pushed `139e03c`. Left `Main.jar` untracked. Session 2 (restart for `Main.jar`): an invalid `gh` command, then stopped |
| Codex (`--tool codex`) | [Rust #1](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb331-c107-78c7-8ff6-9f127a3c593c/issues/1) / [PR #2](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb331-c107-78c7-8ff6-9f127a3c593c/pull/2) | `b8b78e59` | **stopped by the operator, exit 137**, after 14 h 8 min | `main.rs` + verify script, compiled and ran, committed. **Pushed to branch `so`** (fails), then **210** `web_run` calls with `{}` until the sidecar was stopped. No workflow |
| Agent CLI (`--tool agent`) | [Scala #1](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-00e1-73b9-955e-f357a1600d5b/issues/1) / [PR #2](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-00e1-73b9-955e-f357a1600d5b/pull/2) | `2e56df93` | **failed, exit 1** after 2 h 39 min | Nothing new: 7 attempts, each repeated the same reads and writes and stopped at `scalac: not found` |

Goal of this issue: everything Formal AI must change so that the **next release completes all three runs**. Each item below has the evidence from these logs, the related issue if one exists, and a regression test built from this exact input. Parts outside Formal AI are listed at the end and tracked in their own repositories.

This continues #1162 (the same three tasks on 2026-09-27 with 0.352.1) and #1328 (the Codex loop of this run, observed live).

## What went wrong, per task

### 1. Claude Code, Kotlin (`2719fb28`, 14:14 → 14:21 UTC)

1. Session 1 (`858bf47a`, 7 turns) did the work correctly:
   - `gh issue view` (title and body);
   - wrote `Main.kt` and `tests/verify-output.sh`;
   - ran `kotlinc Main.kt -include-runtime -d Main.jar`, then the verify script (`Hello, World!`);
   - `git add … && git commit … && git push -q origin 'issue-1-604f2202fd18'` → `139e03c`, pushed.

   It ended `subtype=success` with "Created and verified `Main.kt` through the agentic CLI harness."
2. **`Main.jar` was left untracked** in the working tree: Formal AI's own build command writes it into the repository root. Hive Mind restarts the session for every uncommitted file (#1157 has the same symptom from 2026-09-27).
3. Session 2 (`539e9b34`, 2 turns) got Hive Mind's restart prompt, which lists `?? Main.jar` and asks to commit, ignore or delete each file. Formal AI did none of that. Its only step was:
   ```
   gh pr view 'https://github.com/…/pull/2' --comments --json comments,reviews
   → Exit code 1: specify only one of --comments or --json
   ```
   It then ended with "Prepared-work continuation stopped at `gh pr view …`". The usage error names the fix (`--json comments,reviews` alone), but Formal AI neither retried it nor moved on to the actual request (`Main.jar`).
4. Hive Mind then stopped with "no progress between sessions" (same HEAD `139e03c`, `Main.jar` still there), exit 1.

The PR content is close to complete: `Main.kt`, the verify script and `.github/workflows/run.yml` (from the 2026-09-27 run) are there, and CI passes. What failed the run is the build output and the second session.

### 2. Codex, Rust (`b8b78e59`, 08:27 → 22:36 UTC)

Details and the live observation are in #1328. Final numbers:

1. 08:41:50: `rustc main.rs -o main`, the verify script passed, and `git commit` succeeded. **`git push -q origin 'so'`** then failed with `error: src refspec so does not match any`. The branch name came from the system prompt's guideline sentence "commit each atomic step … to the pull request **branch so** interrupted work remains preserved". The real branch `issue-1-09b0c76bd0e4` appears 11 times in the same Codex session (`turn_context.git.branch`, the prompt).
2. 08:43:55 → 16:35:10: **210** `codex_apps search_service.web_run` calls, all with `arguments: {}`, all rejected (`InvalidActionArgumentsError … missing_required_argument`). Before every call the text was the same: "Let me search the web for rust src refspec so does not match any." There was no repeat stop. Each answer used 57–140 s of a full core, and the request body grew by 864 B per call.
3. After the sidecar was stopped (16:35:50), Codex waited "for network" until the operator stopped the task at 22:36. Hive Mind then auto-committed and pushed the untracked **`main` binary (4.5 MB)** that Formal AI's `rustc main.rs -o main` had left in the repository root (`693630a`). The same build-output problem as `Main.jar`.
4. **Requirement 6 (a GitHub Actions workflow) was never planned**: the PR has no workflow and no CI.

### 3. Agent CLI, Scala (`2e56df93`, 14:28 → 17:07 UTC)

1. Every attempt repeated the same steps: `gh issue view` ×2, write `Main.scala`, write `tests/verify-output.sh`, `scalac Main.scala` → `/bin/sh: 1: scalac: not found` (exit 127), then stop. There were 7 attempts: the first plus 6 Hive Mind retries of the same session; the last one failed at once on the stopped sidecar. `scalac` ran 8 times. **No commit was made on 2026-10-20**: the PR still has only the September commits.
2. Formal AI never checked which toolchain exists (`command -v scalac`, `scala-cli`, `cs`, `sbt`), never tried a fallback, and never handed compilation to CI (the PR already has a workflow that passes). #1159 is the same failure from 2026-09-15.
3. **The tool's exit code was misread.** The agent CLI's tool result carries `"metadata": {"exit": 127}` and `"error": "Exit code 127\n/bin/sh: 1: scalac: not found"`, yet Formal AI answered "Step `scalac Main.scala` for `Main.scala` failed. **No exit code was reported**, so the verdict rests on what the tool said".
4. A resumed session re-ran the steps the history already showed as done (see #1328, attempts 1–5).
5. 17:07: Hive Mind's retry found the stopped sidecar unreachable and failed the task properly ("the Formal AI endpoint … could not be reached").

### Sidecar, all three runs

- **Logs and memory not written.** During the Claude run alone there were 83 `level error` lines: `[dialog-log] failed to record exchange: Permission denied (os error 13)`, `logging_failed_check_log_directory_permissions_and_space`. There were also `[memory] failed to record live chat exchange: refusing to write an incompatible persisted-memory schema`. The permission part is Hive Mind's volume ownership (link-assistant/hive-mind#3583). **The incompatible persisted-memory schema is Formal AI's**: an existing memory volume from an older version can't be used, and nothing upgrades it (compare #982).
- **`formal-ai serve` ignores SIGTERM.** `docker stop -t 10` ended with exit 137 (#1328).
- **The runs used 0.354.1** although v0.355.0 had been released at 2026-10-19 22:37 UTC, about 10 h before the first run. Its notes mention "Preserve observed tool exit status …", "keep explicitly requested workflow paths in fetched coding tasks" and "Continue missing-command recovery …". So items 4, 6 and 7 below may be partly addressed already, but they are unverified for these inputs.

## What Formal AI must fix (each with a regression test from these logs)

1. **Branch name from the prompt's prose** (`so`). Push to the checked-out branch (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, or the client's `git.branch` context), never to a word taken from guideline text. Test: the exact Codex system prompt and turn context from `b8b78e59` → `git push origin issue-1-09b0c76bd0e4`. (#1328)
2. **Tool calls with empty or invalid arguments, and no repeat stop.** `web_run` must get its `input`/`query`. The same failing call with the same arguments must not be planned again: after the second identical failure, change the plan or end the task with an honest failure. Test: the `b8b78e59` transcript at item 12 ends in ≤ 2 identical calls. (#1328)
3. **Build outputs left in the repository** (`Main.jar`, `main`). Build into a temporary directory, or add a matching `.gitignore` and commit it, or delete the output after verifying. Never leave an untracked file. Test: Kotlin and Rust tasks end with an empty `git status --porcelain`. (#1157)
4. **Hive Mind's continuation prompt.** When the prompt lists uncommitted files, handle each one as asked (commit, ignore or delete) before anything else. A usage error from `gh` (`specify only one of --comments or --json`) must be corrected and retried, or skipped, instead of ending the session. Reading PR feedback must use valid flags (`gh pr view <n> --json comments,reviews`). Test: the `539e9b34` input ends with `Main.jar` ignored or removed, pushed, and a clean tree. (#1158, #1157)
5. **Requirement coverage before success.** Check every numbered requirement of the issue before answering success. Here requirement 6 (a GitHub Actions workflow that builds and runs the program on push and pull request) was never planned for Rust, and for Kotlin and Scala it was never checked against the existing `run.yml`. Test: all three issue bodies → a workflow exists, runs the program and the verify script, and CI is green.
6. **Missing toolchain.** Probe before compiling (`command -v`). If the compiler is missing, use an available alternative or install it in user space (e.g. `scala-cli` / coursier for Scala). As a last resort, commit the source, verify script and workflow and let CI build it, with an honest note that local compilation was not possible. Never stop with the work uncommitted. Test: the Scala issue in an image without `scalac` → the work is committed and CI is green. (#1159)
7. **The agent CLI's tool-result format.** Read `state.metadata.exit` (and `state.error` "Exit code N") from OpenCode-style `tool_use` parts. "No exit code was reported" was false here. Test: the `scalac` result from `2e56df93`. (0.355.0 "Preserve observed tool exit status" may cover this; please confirm with this exact input.)
8. **Resumed sessions.** Continue from the last completed step instead of re-running finished reads, writes and commands. A resume after a completed, committed step should make no further changes. Test: resuming `ses_ea64805c8ffe…` after attempt 1 does not rewrite `Main.scala`. (#1157, #1328)
9. **Evidence files committed into the user's PR.** Both the Kotlin and Rust runs committed `dev/log/self-authored/issue-1/evidence/{claude,codex}-stream.jsonl` as **empty files (0 bytes)**, plus `session-id.txt`. Please decide: either commit them with content (and say so in the PR description), or keep them out of the user's repository. An empty evidence file proves nothing and adds noise to a Hello World PR.
10. **Persisted-memory schema.** Upgrade or migrate an older memory volume unattended and without data loss, or start a new one and say so. Don't refuse every write for the whole session. (#982)
11. **SIGTERM.** `formal-ai serve` should shut down within the stop timeout instead of being killed (exit 137). (#1328)

## Outside Formal AI (tracked in their own repositories)

- **link-assistant/agent:** its own `POST /session/<id>/message` request is reset after ~256 s (255,992 / 256,052 / 256,215 ms). With Formal AI at 60–140 s per step, every session longer than about 4 minutes hits it.
- **link-assistant/hive-mind:**
  - it takes that reset for a transient network failure and resumes the session (Retry 1–6, 3 → 30 min);
  - its `--auto-commit-uncommitted-changes` committed and pushed a 4.5 MB compiled binary;
  - the failed Kotlin run ends with PR #2 ready for review, not draft ("Converting PR: To ready for review (run end (No progress between sessions))");
  - the runs used 0.354.1 although 0.355.0 was out;
  - #3583 (volume ownership).
- **Codex 0.163.0:** with a local provider that is down it waits for the network indefinitely instead of failing the turn.

## Acceptance (the next release)

1. Each fix above has a regression test whose input is taken from these logs (prompts, transcripts, tool results), and the tests run in Formal AI's CI.
2. Against a local `formal-ai serve --agent-mode`, with Claude Code (Kotlin), Codex (Rust) and the Agent CLI (Scala) as clients, using **these three issue bodies and these PR branches**, each run ends with:
   - one program file printing exactly `Hello, World!` with explaining comments and build/run instructions;
   - a verify script and a workflow that runs both on push and pull request, with green CI;
   - no build outputs committed and a clean working tree;
   - everything pushed to the PR branch;
   - the PR description updated and the PR ready;
   - CLI exit 0.

   A second run on the same checkout is a no-op success. No run makes more than 2 identical failing tool calls.
3. Then Hive Mind's `/claude`, `/codex` and `/agent` runs of the same three issues all end with `✅` (exit 0) on the released image.

## Logs (secret gists; the email and Codex `account_id` are redacted)

- Claude Code / Kotlin, execution `2719fb28`, 14:14 → 14:21 UTC: https://gist.github.com/konard/bde1161e75014632ee711c07328f21b9
- Codex / Rust, execution `b8b78e59`, 08:27 → 22:36 UTC: https://gist.github.com/konard/fc014070fb8976cd3ad7766ed0675c0a
- Agent CLI / Scala, execution `2e56df93`, 14:28 → 17:07 UTC: https://gist.github.com/konard/74beb03d2d22bfaf8bb8b96dc6bd73e1
- Formal AI 0.354.1 sidecar stdout, 08:27 → 16:35 UTC: https://gist.github.com/konard/64cec5f80bec8275df4d255399a7e80e
- Codex rollout `01a1586d` (to 15:31 UTC) and earlier logs: in #1328

1446.title: Research & Implementation: Enhancing the Temperature and Randomization Mechanism via ProbabilityStore and Memory Dreaming
1446.body:
### 1. Context & Theoretical Background
Following recent advancements in complexity theory (specifically the RL = L derandomization proof introduced in OpenAI's October 6, 2026 release), it is mathematically established that randomness does not grant additional computational power to bounded-memory algorithms. However, in engineering practice, incorporating controlled randomness (such as temperature) can significantly accelerate solution discovery, prevent local minima entrapment, and balance the trade-offs between strict deterministic exploration and heuristic acceleration.

As a symbolic, deterministic framework built on GOFAI traditions, Formal AI must reflect these principles realistically within its architecture, rather than mimicking LLM hyperparameter concepts on a surface level.

### 2. Current Implementation Analysis & Facts
Based on the current codebase audit:
* **Deterministic Core:** The codebase relies on `rust/src/solver.rs::UniversalSolver`, which executes a strict 11-step loop (from impulse formalization to solution composition) for every prompt.
* **Non-Neural Architecture:** Knowledge is represented as an inspectable semantic network of human-readable links instead of hidden weights.
* **Existing Infrastructure:** The system already defines a `ProbabilityStore` capable of handling append-only Bayesian evidence and Markov transitions.
* **The Policy Gap:** While `ProbabilityStore` ranks symbolic candidate IDs before the temperature/clarify-vs-guess policy runs, the temperature parameter currently has a minimal impact on the runtime complexity and search behavior of the deterministic solvers (`solver.rs` and `solver_unknown_reasoning.rs`). At `temperature = 0`, the system should guarantee high-quality deterministic results (even if it takes longer), while `temperature > 0` should enable accelerated heuristic shortcuts based on probabilistic evidence.

### 3. The Role of Memory Dreaming in Probabilistic Alignment
To make this system truly dynamic and adaptive, the background **`memory dream`** mechanism (tracked under issue #540) must act as the primary engine for updating `ProbabilityStore`. 

While the core server is idle, the dreaming worker should analyze the interaction history with the user and the environment to **increase the baseline probability of obtaining the most relevant answers**. Instead of real-time weight calculations during a hot chat turn, `memory dream` will:
* Aggregate and compress the append-only event log into long-term statistical trends.
* Update Bayesian evidence inside the link-network, prioritizing paths, contexts, and rules that have historically led to verified, high-quality outcomes.
* Mine recurring multi-turn task structures, dynamically updating Markov transition probabilities so that future heuristic searches (`temperature > 0`) lean toward proven contextual pathways.

### 4. Proposed Research Goals
We need to conduct a deep dive into our solver mechanics to make the randomization/temperature behavior realistic and functional:
1. **Define `temperature = 0` Execution Path:** Ensure that at zero temperature, the `UniversalSolver` falls back to complete, exhaustive symbolic path traversal, ensuring maximum precision and deterministic accuracy, accepting the higher time/step cost if necessary.
2. **Implement Probabilistic Acceleration (`temperature > 0`):** Use the `ProbabilityStore` Markov transition weights to greedily prune or prioritize search paths within the link network, mimicking how higher temperature values allow algorithms to jump out of local minima or bypass exhaustive checking.
3. **Bridge Dreaming and ProbabilityStore:** Formally map the output of background `memory dream` analysis onto the active weights of the `ProbabilityStore`.
4. **Verify Contract Stability:** Ensure that enabling/disabling randomness or modifying temperature does not degrade the core symbolic verification pipelines pinned by our regression suites (e.g., HumanEval/MBPP controls, egg rewrite laws).

### 5. Regression Control (`docs_benchmarks.rs`)
To prevent future regressions and enforce the strict operational semantics of temperature settings, we must implement a dedicated unit/integration test within `rust/tests/unit/docs_benchmarks.rs`. This test will:
* Assert that a set of highly connected link subgraphs evaluated at `temperature = 0` successfully traverses all possible branches, returning exact results while validating the step/time cost.
* Assert that the same subgraph evaluated at `temperature > 0` with populated `ProbabilityStore` weights achieves a lower total step count (heuristic acceleration) without violating baseline correctness.
* Ensure any deviation from these committed architectural ledger entries causes a test failure (`rust/tests/unit/docs_benchmarks.rs` enforcement).

### 6. Proposed Action Plan
* Audit `rust/src/solver.rs`, `rust/src/solver_unknown_reasoning.rs`, and the background dreaming worker to map out exact integration points for `ProbabilityStore`.
* Implement the new step-count validation test within `rust/tests/unit/docs_benchmarks.rs`.
* Document the findings and formalize the updated policy under `VISION.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

1455.title: Document command-stream, web-capture and web-search integrations in the associative stack guide
1455.body:
The public ecosystem audit for konard/konard.github.io#33 found direct integrations absent from `docs/associative-tech-stack.md` (checked 2026-10-28). The guide says it names upstream associative components and that manifests/source paths are authoritative.

The current [`rust/Cargo.toml`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/main/rust/Cargo.toml) declares `command-stream = "1.5"`, `web-capture = "0.3.37"` and `web-search = "0.6.0"`. [`package.json`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/main/package.json) declares `@link-assistant/web-search = "0.11.1"`. None is named in the guide.

[`js/web-search-component-entry.js`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/main/js/web-search-component-entry.js) imports `getDefaultProviderIds` and `mergeResults` from the published web-search package, invokes them, and adapts HTTP requests through web-capture. This is executable evidence of runtime integration, rather than catalog membership.

Please document each component's actual boundary, feature/target constraints, source paths, and relationship to knowledge acquisition or command execution. Repository sources: [command-stream](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream), [web-capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture), [web-search](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search).

The wider ecosystem also includes `lino-cache`, `lino-env`, `lino-schema`, `lino-rest-api`, `lino-document-markup-language`, `deduplino`, `links-queue`, `links-logs-vault`, `meta-notation`, `meta-ontology` and `meta-expression`. These are candidates for a clearly separate ecosystem/compatibility section if useful; this audit does **not** claim they are linked into Formal AI. Keep the current distinction between real dependencies and design references.

Evidence and the full personal/organization inventory are being preserved in [PR 34](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/pull/34), `docs/case-studies/issue-33/`.

1483.title: [Bug][P0] Work-item inspection stops before a useful edit: connect evidence, obligations, patch synthesis and independent checks
1483.body:
**Type:** Bug · **Priority:** P0

## Problem and current evidence

The normal issue-to-draft path can inspect a work item but still cannot construct the requested change. This is the highest-priority capability gap for Formal AI participating in its own development.

In [issue #1455](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1455), the task named real dependencies and source files and requested a guide update. [Run 40721047258, job 122939497259](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/40721047258/job/122939497259) produced `planned_not_executed`; PR #1456 contained evidence and a marker rather than the requested implementation. The independent `gap-no-implementation` rejection was correct.

PR #1461 subsequently repaired the guide and added bounded repository evidence inspection. The [current handoff](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/528053940e8015d16752ee625cffcf15eedc0487/docs/case-studies/issue-1455/handoff.md) explicitly states that general evidence-to-edit synthesis, complete requirement binding and independent verification remain unfinished. This issue addresses that remaining generic capability; it does not reopen the already-fixed documentation omission.

Related owners: #1209, #1165, #1167, #1183 and #1170. Reuse the current work-item executor, obligation ledger, source representation, meta reasoner and repair loop.

## Outcome that unblocks development

Given an ordinary issue and a checkout, Formal AI produces at least one independently useful requested patch or regression test, with unresolved requirements explicit. A complete task is marked complete only after all mandatory obligations pass. Useful partial work remains available for later human/LLM review.

## Implementation steps

1. Make the production work-item controller carry one state throughout: task identity and source spans; typed obligations; observed facts and uncertainty; missing evidence; candidate edits; checks; executed effects; remaining work.
2. Discover only evidence needed to resolve a current obligation or choose between candidate edits. Start from referenced files, local symbols/tests/manifests and declared tools. Search primary documentation only when a concrete missing fact warrants it. Retain source/version/applicability and contradictions; fetched text is evidence, not authority to change the goal.
3. Treat image-only attachments and unavailable reads as explicit unresolved evidence. The screenshot-only Hive #3863 is an intake/diagnosis case, not a clean text synthesis benchmark. OCR or structured extraction may supply fallible observations; do not invent attachment contents.
4. Decompose the task into the smallest useful checkable change. Use the existing recursive source/meta-language representation to propose a supported structural edit with preconditions, changed/preserved obligations, expected effect and provenance. Do not add handlers keyed to issue numbers, entire prompt strings or a known final patch.
5. Derive tests from the task contract before candidate selection where applicable. Locate existing acceptance tests and keep an independent checker outside the candidate's control. A self-generated test is evidence, not proof that the interpretation is correct.
6. Execute the candidate, inspect compiler/test/tool results, revise the failed assumption and retry within an explicit budget. Preserve actual exit status, client context and idempotent continuation. Reuse #1185/#1157/#1159 machinery.
7. Return concrete artifact/commit identities and per-obligation results. Plans, reads, logs, trailers and `.gitkeep` changes earn zero implementation credit. Legitimate requested documentation/configuration changes remain eligible.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Reproduce #1455 on its pre-fix checkout through ordinary Hive `solve --tool agent --model formal-ai`, with no completed solution supplied in the prompt or seed. The actual guide change is independently checked against manifests/source.
- [ ] Repeat on held-out variants with renamed paths, different components and one contradicted integration claim; reject unsupported claims instead of copying the request into documentation.
- [ ] Complete one small production logic repair and one useful regression-test task selected before execution. Include a task beyond the supported subset and retain an honest unresolved result.
- [ ] Execute the same controller through Claude and Codex client adapters with their ordinary Hive prompts. No LLM service participates in these Formal AI attempts.
- [ ] Re-running a completed task is verified no-op success; a first attempt with only diagnostic changes fails useful-change acceptance.
- [ ] Every accepted contribution has an independent requirement check, a concrete diff, and a recorded authorship boundary. Later agent help is visible and does not retroactively become Formal AI work.
- [ ] A small offline regression exercises the original failure and the state transitions; hosted native/client qualification is separate.

Start with a declared supported subset and useful partial contributions. Complete universal language understanding or full cross-language equivalence is not a prerequisite for the first useful patch.

## Dependency contract

**Blocked by:** none; this step can start independently.

**Blocks:** #1491, #1170.

Related umbrella issues provide context; their entire broader scope is not an implicit prerequisite.

1548.title: We need to see what we do most wrong, that blocks our vision and plan to fix that
1548.body:
We should create an issue with all open sub-issues, that block our progress on coding (so we go faster to RSI), general question answering and so on.

All steps like formalization and deformalization (naturalization) with meta language should be supported.

We also need to double check our meta algorithm is truly recursive as per our vision in picture of README.

It should be able to discover information as it goes with reasoning, that discovery should be automatically cached, so we use trusted sources to just enough data to understand the task, be able to split it in specific requirements, and formalize it in to tests in required programming language, and reproduce (from internet) or generate new algorithms (if no algorithm on the internet exists), generation of new algorithm should use the same recursive meta algorithm, so we can split it in parts and for each part solve it saparately that may lead to reuse of parts of existing algorithms and so on.

We should also be able to use source code on GitHub for reference (we only use ideas, not copies of files), and for copy of public domain licensed repository, and if user asks or allows we can use other source code respecting its license as library if possible, or copy file with respecting the file with no violation of original requirements.

Our requirements are like axioms or statements with high probability which should define world model or formal system of the task context, meaning, we should derive next logical statements from that.

So if after formalization we have still some unresolved details, we should try multiple ways to resolve them by formally infer missing statements/details from original requirements statements using https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic

We also collect knowledge on the internet and use previous experience for solution of similar or typical tasks to actually infer missing details.

Our system always should prefer to study multiple options, but in all cases, it should calculate probability or fit to the original requirements based on relative-meta-logic and automatically select best option, once selected it may proceed with plan for implementation, and after plan for implementation is defined enough it should be able to actually go and do all the actions in the plan to actually implement it in the target repository or folder.

If something contradicts this vision it should be updated. If there multiple valid options to try our in our research, we should support configuration (switching) between them.

If something is still not detailed enough use this issue's pull requests to update our vision, docs, guidelines and so on, so all blocking and missing description will help us unblock the movement to actual implementation of this vision.

We also must check latest results at (wait for finish if not finished, while doing other tasks):
- https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-00e1-73b9-955e-f357a1600d5b/pull/2 (here I clearly see no Pull Request description was prepared, was not edited, and also CI/CD was not fixed).
- https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb331-c107-78c7-8ff6-9f127a3c593c/issues/1 (at moment of writing the next execution task is in the queue)
- https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-fa49-7c9d-a664-b7ea33bb698a/issues/1 (at moment of writing the next execution task is in the queue)

We also have auto execution of issues with Formal AI via Hive Mind in this repository and also in https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind, so we should collect all failed attempts to solve real GitHub issues by Formal AI, and make sure it can advance them further.

If we have any issues in https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind that blocks our Formal AI to be successfully used on the orchestrator side, that also must be reported, so we should fix them, but Formal AI should not get too much of special treatment, it should operate as any other OpenAI compatible API providing the intelligence via the API by using formal reasoning.

We should replace all hardcoded solutions with solutions that actually use our meta algorithm for all the tasks we already support.

We scope of this issue is documentation and issues planing, so the result here should be documentation changes and issues created/organized (double check we clearly mark all open issues as bug and features and so on), and all critical blockers should be organized in separate parent issue with all dependencies between issues clearly marked as blockers on GitHub.

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
